qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Global athletic brand heritage and multi-decade sports sponsorship scale. Gross margins consistently remain around ~50% across cycles, though operating profitability fluctuates with footwear fashion trends and inventory clearing.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Athletic footwear and apparel face severe fashion-trend cycle risks, hit-franchise saturation (Samba/Gazelle fatigue), and intense market share erosion from agile challenger brands (On, Hoka). High Asian contract manufacturing exposure introduces persistent supply chain and tariff vulnerabilities.
qualitative.evidence: Adidas generates over €21B in revenue across footwear (~50%+), apparel, and accessories. While gross margins have recovered to ~51% under CEO Bjørn Gulden following the termination of the Yeezy partnership, historical GAAP ROIC has been volatile (17.6% in 2019, 4.0% in 2022, -2.1% in 2023, recovering to ~8.5% in 2024). The business model is repeatedly subject to hit-franchise overproduction cycles (Stan Smith, Superstar, Boost, Yeezy, Samba) followed by promotional discounting. Supply chain is heavily dependent on outsourced factories in Vietnam, Indonesia, and China.
